The black-and-yellow striped bollards are very typical of Portugal. The mix of mid-century white residential blocks, tall apartment towers and tiled sidewalks, along with mild-climate trees, points to Porto. The glass-clad office tower in the distance and the overall urban density suggest the Boavista / Campo Alegre area of western Porto.

text:
The A-frame glass-and-steel bar entrance, the "Biggain Tattoo" signage, the tourist souvenir stalls and the old Sino-Thai shophouses are typical of Bangkok's backpacker district. This looks like "The One at Khaosan" complex on Khao San Road in Banglamphu.

>>> {"country":"Thailand","place":"Khao San Road, Bangkok","lat":13.7589,"lng":100.4973}

The Khmer script on the optics shop sign and the dense tangle of overhead wires point clearly to Cambodia. The house plate reads "N.13A St.278", which matches Phnom Penh's numbered street grid. Street 278 runs through the expat-heavy Boeung Keng Kang 1 neighbourhood, and that fits the "Suzy! Time Cafe" and the bicycle parking sign.

>>> {"country":"Cambodia","place":"Phnom Penh, BKK1, Street 278","lat":11.5543,"lng":104.9262}

Suspended street lamps strung over the road, Danish-style sidewalks with granite slabs edged by cobble strips, and dense rows of city bikes all point strongly to Copenhagen. The large uniform 1930s-style office blocks on the left sit behind a sunken cut with railings, which looks like the railway trench near Vesterport station. That suggests Vester Farimagsgade or Kampmannsgade, with Pride flags hanging over the street.

>>> {"country":"Denmark","place":"Copenhagen, Vester Farimagsgade","lat":55.6768,"lng":12.5652}

This is a neoclassical grey limestone building with a Britannia figure in the pediment, and the grey stone neighbours match the 19th-century architecture of Old Montreal. It looks like the Old Custom House (Ancienne-Douane) on Place Royale, now part of the Pointe-à-Callière museum. The red bilingual-style signs and the overcast summer planting fit as well.

>>> {"country":"Canada","place":"Old Montreal, Place Royale, Montreal, Quebec","lat":45.5026,"lng":-73.5541}

guess.place: Old Montreal, Place Royale, Montreal, Quebec

text:
The yellow sedan taxi strongly suggests Tunisia, where taxis are painted yellow. The flat, sunny, dry coastal landscape fits too, along with the modern glass office block, the cranes and the new wide boulevards with tall lamp posts. A European Knaus campervan points to an overlander travelling through North Africa. This kind of new planned business district matches Les Berges du Lac 2 in Tunis.

>>> {"country":"Tunisia","place":"Les Berges du Lac 2, Tunis","lat":36.8450,"lng":10.2720}

The blue bike-share docks carry "EnCicla" branding, which is Medellín's public bicycle system, and a shop sign reads "Medellín". The elevated concrete viaduct is the Medellín Metro, and the blue totem says "San Antonio", the downtown interchange station of Lines A and B. Spanish signs like "Compraventa" and the brick pedestrian paving fit El Centro around San Antonio.

>>> {"country":"Colombia","place":"San Antonio station, Medellín","lat":6.2469,"lng":-75.5700}

text:
The red-and-white articulated bus matches Santiago's Red Metropolitana de Movilidad livery, and the yellow-painted curbs and wide paved median with a bike lane are typical of the Alameda (Av. Libertador Bernardo O'Higgins) in Santiago, Chile. The large white-and-yellow neo-Gothic church on the left looks like the Catedral Evangélica (Jotabeche) on the Alameda in Estación Central, though that identification is my best match rather than certain.

>>> {"country":"Chile","place":"Estación Central, Santiago","lat":-33.4528,"lng":-70.6885}

The blue bike-share bicycle looks like Luxembourg's Vel'oh system. The shop sign appears to read "INOWAI", which I believe is a Luxembourg real estate firm. The 1960s–70s modernist office block, European road markings and wide boulevard beside a wooded park all fit Luxembourg City's ring of boulevards. My best guess is near the Municipal Park along Boulevard Prince Henri or Avenue Émile Reuter, though I'm less sure of the exact street.

>>> {"country":"Luxembourg","place":"Luxembourg City","lat":49.6135,"lng":6.1245}

The trolleybus wires, concrete utility poles, Cyrillic-style road signs (including a "45 / 200м" speed-limit plate) and wide post-Soviet boulevard point to Russia. Several right-hand-drive Japanese cars driving on the right suggest Siberia, where imported used Japanese vehicles are common. The scale of the city and the trolleybus network fit a large Siberian city such as Novosibirsk; the exact street within the city is a rough guess.

>>> {"country":"Russia","place":"Novosibirsk","lat":55.0300,"lng":82.9300}

The Chinese characters "上…物…金属" (Shanghai materials/metals company), the Art Deco stone façade with a large arched door, trolleybus wires, and Santana taxis including a blue Dazhong taxi strongly point to central Shanghai. Old company buildings like this cluster in the Huangpu district north of Nanjing Road, so I'm guessing the Beijing East Road area, with an elevated road visible in the background.

>>> {"country":"China","place":"Shanghai, Huangpu District (Beijing East Road area)","lat":31.2425,"lng":121.4830}

guess.place: Shanghai, Huangpu District (Beijing East Road area)

text:
The Sky Tower spire on the skyline pins this to central Auckland, New Zealand. Traffic keeps left, and the green and blue NZTA-style signs read "City Centre / Downtown" and "SH1 Whangarei / North Shore". Flax plants and pōhutukawa line the road. Those signs suggest a motorway ramp at the edge of the CBD, and the tower's size points to somewhere close, roughly near the Wellington Street/Hopetoun area of the Central Motorway Junction.

>>> {"country":"New Zealand","place":"Auckland CBD, near Central Motorway Junction","lat":-36.8545,"lng":174.7560}

text:
The red gondola overhead is Barcelona's Port Vell aerial cable car (Transbordador Aeri del Port). That fits the right-hand traffic, the tall palm-lined boulevard and the distinctive curved, arched streetlamps along the waterfront. The setting looks like the Ronda del Litoral / Passeig de Colom corridor near Drassanes and Moll de Barcelona, with the old stone port buildings on the left.

text:
Cobblestone paving, ornate black cast-iron street lamps, and dense linden-like street trees are typical of Buenos Aires. Argentine-style plates on a Citroën C3 and the mid-rise apartment blocks with balconies support that. The narrow, leafy residential-commercial street fits central neighbourhoods such as Recoleta or Belgrano; I've chosen Recoleta as the best single guess.

>>> {"country":"Argentina","place":"Buenos Aires, Recoleta","lat":-34.5925,"lng":-58.3960}

text:
The white-painted tree trunks, red-and-white kerbs, reddish soil, palms and ornamental double-headed street lamps on a wide, under-used boulevard strongly suggest Morocco. The gnarled tree in the median looks like an argan or carob, which points towards the Souss plain, though that ID is uncertain. Low, dusty but green surroundings fit a provincial town such as Taroudant, but this could just as easily be another Moroccan town.

>>> {"country":"Morocco","place":"Taroudant, Souss-Massa","lat":30.4703,"lng":-8.8770}

The wide multi-lane boulevard with huge grassy medians, red-brown soil, dry-season grass and a flowering flamboyant tree all point strongly to Brazil's Cerrado. The tall curved modernist streetlights and the low, blocky apartment buildings set back behind lawns are typical of Brasília's planned layout. Right-hand traffic and the Hyundai HB20-type cars fit Brazil. The scene most resembles one of the main axes, like the Eixo Monumental or the L2 road near the Asa Sul/Norte superquadras.

>>> {"country":"Brazil","place":"Brasília, Distrito Federal","lat":-15.7900,"lng":-47.8850}

text:
The vineyard rows on gentle valley slopes, wooded hills, limestone outcrops and a cool central European winter landscape point to southern Germany or northern Switzerland. The green interpretive board with a small logo, the blue "P" sign and the grey cylindrical waste bin fit a German municipal or nature-park setting. Small vineyards next to forested Jura-type terrain suggest Baden-Württemberg, perhaps the upper Neckar valley near Tübingen and Rottenburg, though this is a low-confidence pick.

>>> {"country":"Germany","place":"Rottenburg am Neckar, Baden-Württemberg","lat":48.4770,"lng":8.9350}

The red-brick farmhouse with dark timber cladding, grey concrete paving slabs, a separate asphalt cycle path beside the road, and green double-bar mesh fencing around a school building all point strongly to northern Germany. The flat terrain, lush deciduous trees and rural-suburban edge feel suggest the Hamburg hinterland, most likely Schleswig-Holstein or northern Lower Saxony.

>>> {"country":"Germany","place":"Henstedt-Ulzburg, Schleswig-Holstein","lat":53.7900,"lng":10.0000}

A tropical dry-season landscape with brown grass, deciduous trees and hazy wooded hills points to Central America's Pacific slope. The newly built park infrastructure fits a Central American municipal park: an asphalt jogging path, minimalist concrete benches, a cobblestone drainage swale and a prefab pavilion. The hilly, semi-urban edge with houses on the ridges resembles the San Salvador metro area, possibly Parque Bicentenario.

>>> {"country":"El Salvador","place":"Parque Bicentenario, Antiguo Cuscatlán, San Salvador","lat":13.6830,"lng":-89.2560}

text:
The overcast skies, rendered and stone-faced semi-detached houses with chimneys, and the timber-fenced council playground all point to the British Isles. The style of the modern housing estate and the community-centre building with red trim look typical of Northern Ireland, which leads me to a mid-Ulster or western town.

>>> {"country":"United Kingdom","place":"Omagh, Northern Ireland","lat":54.5977,"lng":-7.3100}

The concrete utility pole, the narrow road with a dashed white centre line and the single-storey pavillon houses with orange-brown tile roofs and rendered walls all point to rural France. The flat, open farmland with a horse paddock, the early-spring vegetation and the style of the subdivision suggest the north-central plains, around Sarthe and Centre-Val de Loire. I'm placing it in Sarthe, near Le Mans.

>>> {"country":"France","place":"Sarthe, Pays de la Loire","lat":48.0500,"lng":0.3500}

Red-tiled roofs over pastel apartment blocks, mixed with houses, sit at the foot of a broad, forested, cloud-capped mountain range. Together with the deciduous greenery, this points to a Balkan town in a valley, most likely in Bulgaria beneath the Stara Planina. The camper van gives no regional clue, but the scale of the town and the way the ridge rises right behind it fit sub-Balkan towns like Karlovo or Sopot.

>>> {"country":"Bulgaria","place":"Karlovo","lat":42.6390,"lng":24.8050}

A Fiat Ducato-based camper van is parked at a small paved rest area with a timber picnic shelter, typical of the Alpine regions. The tall Scots pines mixed with spruce and broadleaf trees suggest a fairly dry inner-Alpine valley. The tidy wooden shelter with its information boards fits a Swiss or French Alpine rest stop, and I lean towards the Valais area of Switzerland.

>>> {"country":"Switzerland","place":"Leuk, Valais","lat":46.3080,"lng":7.6000}

Traffic keeps to the left, and the narrow lane has a white dashed centre line with no edge markings. That points to the British Isles. The banks of bracken, the eucalyptus-like trees, and the heather-topped hill above a patchwork of farmland fit a mild, damp Irish Sea landscape, which leans me toward the Isle of Man. The rounded summit could be North Barrule, which would put this on a lane in the north-east of the island.

>>> {"country":"Isle of Man","place":"Near Ramsey / North Barrule","lat":54.3,"lng":-4.41}

The water tower clearly reads "VENDAS NOVAS", which identifies the town in Portugal's Alentejo region. The flat, sandy terrain, cork and holm oaks, and long low white buildings with red roofs (likely the artillery school complex) fit this location. The open gravel area is probably a fairground or park on the edge of town.

>>> {"country":"Portugal","place":"Vendas Novas, Évora","lat":38.6765,"lng":-8.4560}

The yellow speed sign with an orange border is typical of Iceland. So are the corrugated-iron-clad timber house, the black basalt stone wall and the grey North Atlantic harbour setting. The roundabout right by the waterfront, the anchor display and the rock breakwater suggest an old harbour town on the Reykjanes peninsula. My best guess is the old Duus houses area in Keflavík (Reykjanesbær).

>>> {"country":"Iceland","place":"Keflavík, Reykjanesbær","lat":64.0028,"lng":-22.5585}

Flat terrain with mixed pine and birch forest, right-hand traffic, white edge lines, and white bollards with a black band all fit the Baltics, and they look most like Estonian bollards. The wide main road has a parallel service road and a slip-road junction, which suggests one of Estonia's main highways. The red billboard appears to end in ".ee", which supports Estonia. My best guess is the Tallinn–Tartu highway south-east of Tallinn.

>>> {"country":"Estonia","place":"Tallinn–Tartu highway near Kose, Harju County","lat":59.2,"lng":25.1}

Traffic drives on the right, and the dashed edge lines fit Swedish road markings. The flat terrain, mixed birch woodland and early-spring grey sky suggest south-central Sweden, perhaps the Mälaren/Uppland region.

The flat, grassy roadside suggests the lowland west-coast states, so I'm guessing a village road in Melaka.

Honey-coloured sandstone walls, traditional pebble-mosaic paving and a small marina lined with umbrella-shaded restaurants all point to the eastern Mediterranean. The old round stone tower at the harbour entrance and the horseshoe of waterside cafés match Kyrenia's (Girne's) old harbour in Northern Cyprus.

The "YENI AY" sign is Gagauz Turkish, meaning "new moon", inside an Orthodox Christian setting. That combination points strongly to Gagauzia in southern Moldova. The large yellow church with golden onion domes looks like the Cathedral of St. John the Baptist in Comrat, the region's capital. The older cars, including an Audi 100 and other European models, also fit Moldova.

>>> {"country":"Moldova","place":"Comrat, Gagauzia","lat":46.2985,"lng":28.6565}
